neighbours.label: Best guess: the verb after a readiness or invitation frame ('was willing to hear', 'so please visit and take'), in longer sentences; plain sentences stay quiet.
fire: I told her that her views mattered to me and that I was ready to hear them and answer them.
The exhibit stays until Friday, so please stop by the hall and take a look at it soon.
He felt that the team was prepared to listen and reply to every one of them with care.
The garden is open until June, so please walk over and see it before it closes.
She said that the board was willing to meet them and discuss it at any time.
The book stays on the table, so please come in and read a page or two of it.
We said we were eager to learn from them and work with them over the summer.
The prints are here until May, so please drop in and view them while you can.
quiet: I told her that her coat was on the chair and that the car was parked on the street outside.
The exhibit was large last Friday, and the hall had a lot of old paintings of ships.
He felt that the team was tired after the long trip and the bad weather in the north.
The garden is big and green in June, with many old trees and a pond by the wall.
She said that the board had a long table and a few chairs in the back room.
The book is on the table, next to a lamp and a cup of cold tea and a pen.
We said we were at home with the kids over the summer and that the roof leaked.
The prints are small and grey, with thin frames and a date in the lower corner.

notes: Probes were low everywhere: 0.11-0.22 for these frames in long sentences (0.28 on Chinese '進行', not tested here), and 0.04-0.05 for the same frames and for plain sentences when short. The card has no consistent token (' to', spaces, ' want', ' complied', '進行'). Expected to fail.
